top.description: ORCHARD PARK - Monday night when the Buffalo Bills take on the Minnesota Vikings , Josh Allen will be back at the place where his legend first began taking shape. Buffalo’s only previous visit to U.S. Bank Stadium came in Week 3 of the 2018 season, and for Allen it was just his second NFL start. The odds were stacked against him and the Bills, literally, as the wise guys in Las Vegas installed the Bills as 17-point underdogs. But the newbie quarterback stunned NFL nation and during the Bills’ 27-6 blowout victory , he authored the first of probably about 100 meme-worthy plays, his never-to-be-forgotten leap over Vikings linebacker Anthony Barr . From that moment on he’s been a nonstop highlight reel. As is typically his way, he didn’t have much to say about the play because, as we’ve learned, Allen is very much a live-in-the-moment kind of guy, not one to dwell on past performances. “Honestly, not really,” he said when he was asked if it had crossed his mind that he’s returning to the scene of that first big play. But he did eventually elaborate when he was asked again about whether he was surprised by the crazy reaction that play got on social media with all the memes and later the t-shirts that were emblazoned with the picture of him leaping over Barr. "Surprised me, too," he said. "I was a good athlete in college. High school I was not. So as I got older and started to lift more weights, I guess I got a little more athletic. But yeah, I think it was just kind of a surprising thing for me too of what I was able to do, especially early on in the career with the running stuff. I know I still run a little bit now, but that was I think the moment that I was like, 'You know what? I do belong here.'" He then immediately spun forward and talked about how playing there will be nice in that there won’t be any weather to worry about, though it will be a difficult environment because of the Vikings’ passionate supporters who make that dome among the loudest venues in the NFL. “They're going to be a loud fan base,” he said. “Them being what their record is and kind of rolling right now, and their defense is playing outstanding football, so we're expecting an extremely loud crowd. That's a really, really good crowd. That's what I do remember about being there, early in that game just how loud it was, and they've got their Skol chant, which is an awesome tradition. top.title: The missing piece that Roberto De Zerbi must slot into place after Tottenham's puzzling start
top.description: Tottenham arrived at Elland Road with three consecutive wins and departed disappointed by their failings in three departments. “We did not show character, we did not show personality, we did not show courage,” lamented Roberto De Zerbi and, if he was discussing the second half at Leeds, they amounted to fundamental failings for him. The temptation is to take a swipe at the forward line and say they were found wanting in three other areas: left winger, right winger and centre-forward. That is probably unfair on Mohammed Kudus , a considerable talent only a few starts into a comeback, and cruel to Mathys Tel , taken off before half-time with what De Zerbi fears is a bad injury. Spurs can argue that picking on those charged with scoring is harsh, given that they had seven goals from their three previous games before a powderpuff attack barely threatened Leeds. But the facts show that only Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland have scored fewer in the Premier League - and that may change after Sunday’s games. Only three of Spurs’ 10 have come from forwards: Dominic Solanke ’s injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford, Omar Marmoush’s thunderbolt against Coventry and Tel’s glorious solo goal at Chelsea. A case of quality rather than quantity, perhaps, even if they could all be damned by comparisons with the Ballon d’Or winner who used to deliver both for Spurs; that said, Harry Kane is on a four-game goal drought for Bayern Munich. It may be one of the few ways that Marmoush, whose own drought spans a mere three matches, ranks better than Kane. Yet the Egyptian is the face of a conundrum Spurs have created with their record outlay; while those three victories offered encouraging evidence that De Zerbi’s buys are having an impact in defence and midfield, the attacking acquisitions were Marmoush and Savio, who have a combined tally of one goal and no assists in the top flight. The Brazilian has not played for four weeks but, between them, they will earn Manchester City £145m. City seem to have got much the better of those deals. Savio has always faced the question of whether he can be productive enough and if he is best suited to the left or the right, Kudus’ best position. Marmoush increasingly faces the question of what he is: neither really a striker nor a winger. The Egyptian was prolific for Eintracht Frankfurt in a strike duo, alongside Hugo Ekitike; but De Zerbi does not play two up front. Solanke, more of a conventional spearhead, has four goals in his last 25 league games. top.title: Football match remembers WW1 Christmas truce
top.description: It was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play [BBC] A football match commemorating the World War One Christmas truce has taken place in Nottinghamshire. On Christmas Day 1914, British and German troops stopped fighting and met at several locations in Belgium. A soldier from Newark, William Setchfield, was present at one near the village of Messines and he may have provided the football used during the truce. On Saturday, Newark Town played a side from its twin town of Emmendingen in what was billed a Peace Match. Luke Parsons, manager of Newark Town FC, said: "We've played previously. It's two histories, two cultures coming together to symbolise the friendship of what we are about." He added: "Obviously that was put down 108 years ago and we want to continue that with this game." The two teams have played each other twice before at the site of the front lines in Belgium for the centenary of the event. However, this was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play. Parsons said: "It makes me incredibly proud to invite them over to England to fulfill another fixture." A replica World War One era football was exchanged between the teams [BBC] Jakob Griessbaum, captain of Emmendingen FC, said the team was "honoured" to visit and play in the match. "It's a nice opportunity for us to get together," he added. "We are happy to play football, to think about World War One and what happened there." Francis Towndrow, local historian for Newark Town FC, who was at the game, said the score in the two previous encounters was 4-1 to the German team, and then 2-2, but Newark won on penalties. "The Germans have been itching to play again to beat us so it's wonderful they are here," he added. The final score of the game, played at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way on Saturday, was a 2-0 win to Newark. The Blues thanked Emmendingen and wished them "safe travels home", adding: "Thank you to all that came out to support. "Football is the winner. Fantastic to be a part of." The Peace Match kicked off at 14:00 GMT at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way [BBC] Towndrow said research had revealed accounts of how good Setchfield was as a goalkeeper. He added: "We can from that deduce that he may have played in goal that day and also that [the] football he got for Christmas was used." Towndrow said Setchfield survived the war and stayed in the Nottinghamshire area. He died in 1959 at the age of 71. top.title: Cincinnati provides update on JV Gibson injury
top.description: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 07: Cincinnati Bearcats receiver JV Gibson tries to break free of a Houston Cougars defender during the second quarter of a college football game between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars on Saturday, November 07, 2026 at TDECU Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With roughly seven minutes remaining in a heated Big 12 showdown between Cincinnati and Houston, the atmopshere inside TDECU Stadium abruptly changed. The crowd fell silent, and the passion and energy inside the building quickly turned into concern. Cincinnati wide receiver JV Gibson suffered a frightening collision with Houston strong safety Jordan Allen while running a post route toward the end zone. The impact left Cincinnati’s leading receiver motionless on the field, prompting officials to throw flags for pass interference and targeting penalties. But the officiating decisions quickly became secondary. As Gibson remained down with an apparent head injury, medical personnel rushed onto the field to attend the receiver. Members of the Cincinnati roster left the sideline to gathered around their teammate, kneeling nearby as trainers continued their evaluations. Gibson’s parents eventually made their way to the field as well. The game was delayed 16 minutes as medical personnel stabilized Gibson, placed him on a stretcher, and transported out of TDECU Stadium. His father accompanied him on the back of the medical cart. Gibson subsequently made his way to Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center. Before his departure, Cincinnati Athletics reported the receiver as “alert and moving all extremities.” “Our personnel did an amazing job to get out there very quickly, they were right on top of JV,” Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield said in the immediate aftermath of the game. “Ultimately, they got him in a good place there. He was moving all four extremities on command. They took him to the hospital for precautionary reasons, and obviously they got to do their CT scans and those type of things. I don’t have an update, but hopefully everything checks out great. I thought JV was playing awesome tonight and unfortunately that happened to him. Prayers go out to JV and his family, but it’s a blessing for him to move all four extremities. It’s always very scary, and scary for our team.” In a later update, Cincinnati’s official Twitter account confirmed that Gibson had been discharged from Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center and traveled back to Cincinnati with the team.

top.title: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories
top.description: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories Real Madrid have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past month, and the results have been there for everyone to see. Los Blancos secured a 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla last night to make it eight wins in their last eight games. Jose Mourinho’s tactical modifications have worked wonders for the Spanish club, and the performances have also improved. According to MARCA , he has moulded the team into a more cohesive and disciplined unit after a difficult start to his second spell in the Spanish capital. Mourinho’s Real Madrid growing stronger collectively Madrid have scored 24 goals across those eight matches, averaging three per game, while keeping three clean sheets. The winning run includes victories over Barcelona in El Clasico and Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the Champions League. Saturday’s 3-0 victory over Valencia offered another example of their progress, with the team breaking down a resolute defensive unit. Jose Mourinho has galvanized the team at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Los Che actually started the game very well, causing problems for Madrid, but goals from Fede Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe helped Mourinho’s men secure the three points. The most encouraging aspect of Real Madrid’s evolution is that the team no longer seem excessively dependent on individual brilliance. Mbappe, Guler, Diomande and Bellingham have come together to form an excellent attacking quartet, and their strengths complement each other perfectly. Mourinho’s defensive demands making the difference There was one moment in the Valencia game that perfectly summed up the defensive transformation under Mourinho. When Guler was caught out of position after Madrid lost possession, Mbappe sprinted across to cover the exposed space and restore the team’s defensive shape. One of the biggest criticisms levelled at the Frenchman was that he was not contributing enough defensively. How will Mourinho integrate Vinicius into the team? (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) That has changed now, with everyone willing to put the team ahead of themselves. Mourinho will love the fact that his side have almost reached that stage. It remains to be seen how the dynamics change once Vinicius Jr. returns from suspension and how the manager reintegrates him. If the team can find a way for Vinicius to thrive within this system too, they could become even more devastating in the coming months. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles his return.

top.title: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent
top.description: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano this weekend for one of the most important matches of the season. It promises to be an important game for many of the Barcelona players, including the new signing Anthony Gordon, who will play his first competitive game at the Metropolitano. Barcelona’s poor record against Atleti last season has already been well-documented , but this particular game is even more important for Gordon, who has had a bad precedent as well. The poor precedent Can Gordon make an impact against Atletico Madrid? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported by Diario SPORT , Gordon has faced Atletico Madrid only once in his career. It was in August last year in the Sepa Cup, and it wasn’t the best of experiences for the winger. Deployed through the middle as Newcastle United slipped to a 2-0 defeat, it was a bruising afternoon for Gordon. The Englishman found fierce resistance from the Atleti defence and was eventually forced off in the 85th minute due to ankle discomfort. This could be an early reminder that Diego Simeone’s men could employ the same method when it comes to putting a halt to Gordon in the final third. This time, however, the Barcelona player will operate from the flanks, which should give the Englishman a higher degree of freedom. Pressure slowly growing Godon needs to up his performances once again. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) With three goals and five assists in all competitions, it will be perhaps unfair to criticise Gordon’s performances since joining Barcelona in the summer. The winger has won his battle with Karim Adeyemi for the left wing role, and established himself as a first-team regular. Yet, question marks remain. Gordon notably endured a poor outing against Real Madrid in the season’s first El Clasico and is still yet to score his first away goal in La Liga. His only goals in La Liga so far have come at home against Getafe and Alaves. That is quite a modest tally for a player of his quality. A strong performance against Atletico Madrid, to that end, could serve as an ideal confidence-booster for the former Newcastle United starlet, as he looks to solidify his role in Flick’s setup.

Every IPL trade update ahead of the 2027 mini-auction Franchises across the Indian Premier League are inching closer to finalising their retention lists for the 2027 season, with the mini-auction scheduled for December. Before that auction window opens, several teams are expected to explore trade routes first, swapping players outright or settling deals purely in cash, as a quicker way to patch up squad gaps before bidding even begins. Over the years, several marquee names, including Hardik Pandya, Robin Uthappa and Cameron Green, have switched franchises through trade deals rather than the auction table. nigeria.title: Iran executes three men linked to anti-government protests
nigeria.description: Iranian authorities have executed three men convicted of carrying out operations on behalf of Israel and the United States during anti-government protests in January, the country’s judiciary has announced. The death sentences against Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh were carried out on Sunday after being upheld by the Supreme Court, the judiciary’s Mizan Online website reported. According to the report, the three men were found guilty of “participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups” during the protests. Mizan said the defendants threw Molotov cocktails and grenades, used bladed weapons and firearms, and set fire to public facilities in Karaj, a city west of Tehran. Other defendants in the case received prison sentences ranging from five to 10 years, the report added. The protest movement, which initially erupted in December over the rising cost of living, rapidly developed into widespread anti-government demonstrations that peaked on January 8 and 9. Iranian authorities reported more than 3,000 deaths during the unrest, blaming the violence on what they described as “terrorist acts” orchestrated by the United States and Israel. However, foreign-based non-governmental organisations have reported higher casualty figures and maintained that Iranian security forces fired on protesters. The number of executions in Iran has increased since the outbreak of the Middle East war, which was triggered in late February by US and Israeli strikes on the Islamic Republic. nigeria.title: Israeli president Herzog picks Eisenkot to form new government
nigeria.description: Israeli President Isaac Herzog has chosen opposition leader and former military chief, Gadi Eisenkot, to form a new government following an election that left both his camp and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s coalition short of a parliamentary majority. Herzog’s office announced on Saturday night that the president had informed Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, of his intention to give him the mandate to form a government. The formal appointment is expected to take place at a ceremony at the president’s residence in Jerusalem on Sunday. “This is the time to establish a national emergency government. I will do anything possible to prove us worthy,” Eisenkot wrote on X following the announcement. The decision brings Eisenkot closer to replacing Netanyahu, Israel’s longest-serving prime minister, after the religious-nationalist coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October 27 election. Netanyahu’s camp secured 54 seats in the 120-member parliament, while Eisenkot’s opposition bloc won 48, leaving both short of the 61 seats required to form a government. During consultations with Herzog, Eisenkot received endorsements from two Arab-majority political lists, whose support could prove crucial in the coalition-building process. However, uncertainty remains over whether Eisenkot’s bloc would accept a formal alliance with the Arab-led parties, particularly after more than three years of war in Gaza. Netanyahu has opposed any arrangement involving the Arab parties, accusing them of supporting terrorism and warning against forming a government with what he described as “terrorist supporters”. He has also called for a national unity government. Eisenkot, however, has indicated a willingness to work with Arab-led parties under certain conditions, including their acceptance that Hamas is a terrorist organisation that must be dismantled. He has also pledged to take action against extremist Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank accused of attacking Palestinians, describing the incidents as “Jewish terror” allegedly enabled by Netanyahu’s government. Despite his willingness to engage with Arab-led parties, Eisenkot opposes the creation of a Palestinian state. He has also vowed to end Hamas’ rule in Gaza and destroy its military wing. Eisenkot served as Israel’s Chief of General Staff from 2015 to 2019 and commanded the military during the 2006 war with Hezbollah. During the conflict, he developed the so-called “Dahiya doctrine”, a military strategy advocating the use of overwhelming force against civilian infrastructure in areas controlled by Hezbollah. Under the Israeli constitutional process, Eisenkot has 28 days to secure the support of at least 61 lawmakers and form a government. Herzog can grant him an additional 14 days if he fails to meet the deadline. If Eisenkot cannot secure a parliamentary majority within the allotted period, the president may offer the mandate to another candidate. Failure by any candidate to form a government

nigeria.description: By Enitan Abdultawab The Women in Management, Business and Public Service (WIMBIZ) has renewed its push for greater participation of women in business and leadership, identifying mentorship, visibility and empowerment as key tools for helping women access opportunities and advance their careers. The Executive Head of WIMBIZ, Omowunmi Akingbohungbe, said the organisation was committed to inspiring and empowering women to attain leadership positions while equipping them to become entrepreneurs. Speaking during an interview at the organisation’s 25th annual conference in Lagos, Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ connects experienced and accomplished women with emerging leaders to guide them through the challenges of building careers and businesses. “We’re big on mentoring. We connect mentors, accomplished and experienced women with rising leaders so they can handhold them and show them the path so they’re not reinventing the wheel,” she said. She also stressed the importance of visibility, noting that women needed to make their abilities known, develop confidence and put themselves forward for leadership opportunities. According to her, many women often hold back from applying for leadership positions because they feel they are not qualified, whereas men are more likely to take the chance. “Most times women will think I’m not qualified and all of that, but men would apply. And we also have the potential,” she said. Akingbohungbe said WIMBIZ was therefore working to ensure women recognise their capabilities and have the confidence to pursue opportunities in business and public service. “At WIMBIZ, we train, mentor, empower women. We give women a right to be entrepreneurs at the same time,” she added. She described the organisation’s partnership with Autos, its official automobile partner for the annual conference, as part of its 25th anniversary celebrations. She said the partnership would also provide discounts to WIMBIZ members and free vehicle servicing for two years. Nigeria secured the title through goals from Oluebube Umejiaku and Awawu Bashiru, while Fuki Ito scored for Japan. Reacting after the encounter, Shirai acknowledged Nigeria’s superiority but maintained that his players gave their best throughout the final. “First of all, I have to say that Nigeria were a very strong team. We understood their strengths, but there were moments when they managed to get in behind our defence. Even so, I think our players fought incredibly hard until the very end, doing everything they could to cope with Nigeria’s speed and physical power. I also believe that if we had managed to score earlier, we might have had a better chance of winning the match. I want them [Japan’s players] to be proud of themselves. The way they fought until the very end of this World Cup will have inspired many people, and I hope they can take confidence from that,” Shirai said. Japan reached the final after defeating DPR Korea in the semi-finals, while Nigeria booked their place in the title decider with a victory over Brazil. The Flamingos eventually defeated Japan to claim the U-17 Women’s World Cup trophy, marking a historic achievement for Nigerian women’s football. The commission said it would not take a position on the party’s leadership crisis until it obtained and examined the Certified True Copy (CTC) of the judgment. The Federal High Court in Abuja had, on Thursday, nullified the Mark-led caretaker committee and invalidated decisions taken under its leadership, including the party’s presidential primary that produced Atiku as its candidate for the 2027 general elections. Speaking on Sunday, INEC National Commissioner and Chairman of its Information and Voter Education Committee, Mohammed Haruna, said the commission would not rely on media reports to determine the court’s position. “We can’t take a position until we see the judgment ourselves. We have to get the Certified True Copy because we don’t take decisions or reports of what the court said based on reports because the reports could be wrong,” he said. Haruna added that the commission would deliberate on the matter at its meeting next week. “Well, this one is very straightforward. Even then, we are all here till next week when the commission meets. We will have to meet over it,” he said. He also said INEC would comply with any further court order arising from an appeal by the Mark-led faction. “Obviously, if the David Mark faction should appeal, which I am sure they will, and they get an injunction for stay of execution, obviously, we’ll have to obey that judgment,” he added. nigeria.title: Two waterway accidents kill police officer, woman in Bayelsa
nigeria.description: By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa Two separate waterway accidents in Bayelsa State have claimed the lives of a serving police officer and a female passenger, the state Police Command has confirmed. The incidents occurred in Brass and Sagbama Local Government Areas, according to a statement issued on Saturday night by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Musa Mohammed. The first accident involved a passenger boat that capsized along the Abedigbene waterways in Brass LGA on Thursday while travelling from Yenagoa to Akassa with eight persons on board, including a serving commissioner. The police said Maritime Union workers in Brass reported the incident, prompting a search-and-rescue operation by personnel of the Nigerian Navy’s Forward Operating Base (FOB) FORMOSO, in collaboration with local divers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community. Seven passengers were rescued, including the Bayelsa State Commissioner for Trade and Commerce, Dr Ebiere Jones, and an officer of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps. However, a serving police officer who was initially reported missing was subsequently confirmed dead. The second accident occurred at about 5:20 a.m. on Saturday, November 7, along the shoreline of Angalabiri Community in Sagbama LGA, when a tanker vessel belonging to Sterling Global Oil Ltd reportedly collided with canoes navigating close to the shoreline. According to the police, preliminary investigations indicated that the vessel struck and destroyed some of the canoes. One of the victims, identified as Mrs Victoria Abetnigo, an indigene of Angalabiri, sustained serious injuries and was rushed to Ebedebiri General Hospital for treatment. She was, however, pronounced dead by the attending doctor. Her remains have been deposited at Ofoni Mortuary, while investigations are ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident. Reacting to the two tragedies, the Commissioner of Police, Bayelsa State Command, CP Ajao Saka Adewale, expressed sadness over the incidents and extended his condolences to the families, colleagues and loved ones of the deceased. The police commissioner particularly lamented the death of the serving police officer, praying for the peaceful repose of the souls of the deceased and strength for their families to bear the losses. He also commended the Nigerian Navy’s FOB FORMOSO, local divers, Maritime Union workers and members of the Abedigbene fishing community for their prompt intervention during the rescue operation. Adewale urged boat operators and commercial vessel owners to exercise caution and comply strictly with maritime safety regulations. He specifically called on vessel operators to maintain safe distances from shorelines and established canoe routes and avoid reckless navigation. He also advised passengers to wear life jackets throughout their journeys and urged all waterway users to prioritise safety and promptly report emergencies to the appropriate authorities. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine U.S. Treasury Cuts Off MEXC From U.S. Financial System Over Alleged $16 Billion in Illicit Flows The U.S. Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network issued a final order Friday that will cut offshore exchange MEXC Global off from the American banking system over alleged links to sanctions evasion by Iran, North Korea and Russia, the department said . FinCEN’s order, published as a PDF pending Federal Register placement, finds MEXC a “primary money laundering concern in connection with Russian illicit finance” under section 9714(a) of the Combating Russian Money Laundering Act. Thirty days after that Register notice, covered U.S. financial institutions will be barred from any funds transfer — including convertible virtual currency — to or from MEXC. Reuters reported the same cut-off Friday afternoon. Treasury framed the move as part of Operation Economic Outcast. It is not an OFAC sanctions designation: the order says it does not rewrite Bank Secrecy Act duties or OFAC rules, and it is a FinCEN funds-transmittal ban rather than a Section 311 proposed rulemaking. Treasury alleges MEXC facilitated at least $16 billion in illicit flows from May 2021 through May 2026, including nearly $1.5 billion tied to Russian sanctions evasion and about $22 million linked to Iran’s Central Bank and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps’ Qods Force. The platform was still processing trades with sanctioned Garantex and successor Grinex as recently as June 2026, more than four years after OFAC designated Garantex, the release says. What the order does — and when The order , signed by FinCEN Deputy Director Jimmy L. Kirby, covers MEXC Global and named affiliates operating outside the United States, including Seychelles-incorporated MEXC Global Ltd / MX Global Ltd, Estonia’s MEXC Estonia OÜ, Switzerland’s GIDA Technology AG and the U.K.’s MXC Global Ltd, plus successors. Covered institutions face civil or criminal penalties for willful violations. Until the Federal Register publishes the notice, the 30-day clock has not started. As of Friday evening eastern time the Register’s public index still showed no MEXC document, matching the order’s own cover note that publication is pending. Background on MEXC Founded in 2018 and formerly branded MXC, MEXC ranks among the world’s 20 largest centralized crypto venues by volume. Treasury puts daily turnover above $1 billion and reserves near $5 billion as of mid-2026, with access claimed across more than 170 countries. The exchange already lists the United States as a prohibited jurisdiction in its user terms, so Friday’s action mainly hits any remaining dollar rails, banking partners and counterparties that still touch U.S. institutions. Regulators elsewhere have been circling for years. The U.K. Financial Conduct Authority put MEXC Global Ltd on its warning list in March 2024 as unauthorized. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. For its latest limited edition, Maison Martell has brought together Nigerian music superstar Davido and Ghanaian visual artist Prince Gyasi to create a new expression of its prestigious XO cognac , inspired by the sound, movement and global influence of Afrobeats. The Martell Afrobeats Limited Edition XO will be unveiled in Nigeria on November 6, following the collection’s global launch in New York on October 28. At the heart of the collaboration is Prince Gyasi’s distinctive artistic language. Known for his vibrant colours and imaginative compositions, Gyasi has created an original artwork of Davido that features on the limited-edition bottle and presentation box. The design draws inspiration from the landscapes of West Africa, bringing together Martell’s iconic blue with shades of amber and gold. The blue reflects the rhythmic flow of the ocean, while the golden tones evoke sunlit sands and the warmth of African sunsets. As Davido says, ‘We rise by lifting others,’ a reminder that music builds community and lifts us all. I feel a deep pride in Afrobeats, its incredible journey, and the mark it’s making on global music,” Prince Gyasi said. He further explained the thinking behind the colours and composition: “Inspired by the landscapes of West Africa, I blended Martell’s iconic blue with the rhythmic flow of the ocean, golden sands, and waves reimagined in a hyper-surreal style, bringing sound and movement to life. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. No matter what you are starting over at, you have something that can be transferred from where you were to where you are or where you want to be. Adopt a growth mindset In today’s world, flexibility, adaptability and agility are your currencies for greatness. A critical part of thriving through a transition, a pivot or when you are starting over is to be honest about your limits. These could be the limits of your existing knowledge, expertise, and others. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. sports.title: The missing piece that Roberto De Zerbi must slot into place after Tottenham's puzzling start
sports.description: Tottenham arrived at Elland Road with three consecutive wins and departed disappointed by their failings in three departments. “We did not show character, we did not show personality, we did not show courage,” lamented Roberto De Zerbi and, if he was discussing the second half at Leeds, they amounted to fundamental failings for him. The temptation is to take a swipe at the forward line and say they were found wanting in three other areas: left winger, right winger and centre-forward. That is probably unfair on Mohammed Kudus , a considerable talent only a few starts into a comeback, and cruel to Mathys Tel , taken off before half-time with what De Zerbi fears is a bad injury. Spurs can argue that picking on those charged with scoring is harsh, given that they had seven goals from their three previous games before a powderpuff attack barely threatened Leeds. But the facts show that only Nottingham Forest, Crystal Palace and Sunderland have scored fewer in the Premier League - and that may change after Sunday’s games. Only three of Spurs’ 10 have come from forwards: Dominic Solanke ’s injury-time equaliser at Old Trafford, Omar Marmoush’s thunderbolt against Coventry and Tel’s glorious solo goal at Chelsea. A case of quality rather than quantity, perhaps, even if they could all be damned by comparisons with the Ballon d’Or winner who used to deliver both for Spurs; that said, Harry Kane is on a four-game goal drought for Bayern Munich. It may be one of the few ways that Marmoush, whose own drought spans a mere three matches, ranks better than Kane. Yet the Egyptian is the face of a conundrum Spurs have created with their record outlay; while those three victories offered encouraging evidence that De Zerbi’s buys are having an impact in defence and midfield, the attacking acquisitions were Marmoush and Savio, who have a combined tally of one goal and no assists in the top flight. The Brazilian has not played for four weeks but, between them, they will earn Manchester City £145m. City seem to have got much the better of those deals. Savio has always faced the question of whether he can be productive enough and if he is best suited to the left or the right, Kudus’ best position. Marmoush increasingly faces the question of what he is: neither really a striker nor a winger. The Egyptian was prolific for Eintracht Frankfurt in a strike duo, alongside Hugo Ekitike; but De Zerbi does not play two up front. Solanke, more of a conventional spearhead, has four goals in his last 25 league games. Tottenham's forward line needs to find their rhythm in order to improve their results (Getty) Tottenham have a host of imperfect options on the left – Savio, Tel, Marmoush – and if the 18-year-old Luca Williams-Barnett can generate the most excitement, that is in part an indictment of others when he has only played nine minutes of first-team football. sports.title: Football match remembers WW1 Christmas truce
sports.description: It was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play [BBC] A football match commemorating the World War One Christmas truce has taken place in Nottinghamshire. On Christmas Day 1914, British and German troops stopped fighting and met at several locations in Belgium. A soldier from Newark, William Setchfield, was present at one near the village of Messines and he may have provided the football used during the truce. On Saturday, Newark Town played a side from its twin town of Emmendingen in what was billed a Peace Match. Luke Parsons, manager of Newark Town FC, said: "We've played previously. It's two histories, two cultures coming together to symbolise the friendship of what we are about." He added: "Obviously that was put down 108 years ago and we want to continue that with this game." The two teams have played each other twice before at the site of the front lines in Belgium for the centenary of the event. However, this was the first time Emmendingen FC had come to Newark to play. Parsons said: "It makes me incredibly proud to invite them over to England to fulfill another fixture." A replica World War One era football was exchanged between the teams [BBC] Jakob Griessbaum, captain of Emmendingen FC, said the team was "honoured" to visit and play in the match. "It's a nice opportunity for us to get together," he added. "We are happy to play football, to think about World War One and what happened there." Francis Towndrow, local historian for Newark Town FC, who was at the game, said the score in the two previous encounters was 4-1 to the German team, and then 2-2, but Newark won on penalties. "The Germans have been itching to play again to beat us so it's wonderful they are here," he added. The final score of the game, played at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way on Saturday, was a 2-0 win to Newark. The Blues thanked Emmendingen and wished them "safe travels home", adding: "Thank you to all that came out to support. "Football is the winner. Fantastic to be a part of." The Peace Match kicked off at 14:00 GMT at the YMCA centre in Lord Hawke Way [BBC] Towndrow said research had revealed accounts of how good Setchfield was as a goalkeeper. He added: "We can from that deduce that he may have played in goal that day and also that [the] football he got for Christmas was used." Towndrow said Setchfield survived the war and stayed in the Nottinghamshire area. He died in 1959 at the age of 71. According to Caught Offside , the Brighton goalkeeper is attracting close attention after a strong campaign in which he has continued to enhance a growing reputation in the Premier League. The Dutch international, still only 24, is viewed by a number of leading clubs as a high-upside option with both top-flight pedigree and significant room for further development. Bart Verbruggen on Liverpool shortlist Liverpool’s interest appears to fit a broader piece of succession planning. Verbruggen has produced impressive numbers this season, recording 11 clean sheets in 14 appearances across all competitions, and that output has helped place him firmly on the radar of clubs operating at the top end of the market. The sense around this situation is that Liverpool have tracked him for some time rather than reacting only to a short burst of form. That is often how recruitment decisions of this scale are shaped, with long-term monitoring, character checks and tactical suitability all carrying weight before any formal move is explored. Alisson future creates transfer focus What sharpens the issue is uncertainty around Alisson. The report states Liverpool are preparing for the possibility of the Brazilian leaving next summer, which naturally places greater urgency on identifying credible alternatives. When a first-choice goalkeeper enters a delicate contract position, clubs rarely leave succession work until late in the process. Photo: IMAGO Verbruggen’s profile is appealing for obvious reasons. He has experience in England, he is young enough to grow into the role, and he has shown composure at a club where goalkeepers are regularly asked to contribute in and out of possession. Brighton goalkeeper faces elite competition Any deal would be far from straightforward. Manchester United, Chelsea, Bayern Munich and Real Madrid are all said to be monitoring Verbruggen, underlining the level of regard for him across Europe. Liverpool may therefore need to move decisively if their interest develops into something more concrete. At this stage, there is no suggestion of an advanced move, but the logic is easy to follow. If Liverpool are preparing for change in goal, Verbruggen looks like one of the more credible long-term options available. sports.description: Elversberg take record-breaking crowd to Borussia Dortmund Elversberg took 8,000 fans to the Signal Iduna Park for their Bundesliga clash against Borussia Dortmund. Although suffering a 2-1 defeat, their fourth in 2026/27, memories will have been created to last a lifetime for generations of Elversberg’s travelling contingent. But what makes the figure more impressive, is that it’s a club record for Elversberg, who had never played higher than Germany’s 3. Liga until 2023. Additionally, the 8,000 travelling supporters makes up 61 percent of the town’s population – it really is that small! Speaking prior to Elversberg’s trip to Elversberg, head coach Vincent Wagner said: “Hooray, the whole community is here.” And despite being 2-0 down thanks to Felix Nmecha’s second-half brace , Noel Futkeu’s 81st-minute bicycle kick almost kickstarted a comeback. Defeat at the Signal Iduna Park leaves the Saarland club on 13 points from a possible 27 after nine matchdays, a commendable tally for a club that was playing in Germany’s fourth tier in 2022. sports.title: Cincinnati provides update on JV Gibson injury
sports.description: HOUSTON, TX - NOVEMBER 07: Cincinnati Bearcats receiver JV Gibson tries to break free of a Houston Cougars defender during the second quarter of a college football game between the Cincinnati Bearcats and Houston Cougars on Saturday, November 07, 2026 at TDECU Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by Austin McAfee/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images With roughly seven minutes remaining in a heated Big 12 showdown between Cincinnati and Houston, the atmopshere inside TDECU Stadium abruptly changed. The crowd fell silent, and the passion and energy inside the building quickly turned into concern. Cincinnati wide receiver JV Gibson suffered a frightening collision with Houston strong safety Jordan Allen while running a post route toward the end zone. The impact left Cincinnati’s leading receiver motionless on the field, prompting officials to throw flags for pass interference and targeting penalties. But the officiating decisions quickly became secondary. As Gibson remained down with an apparent head injury, medical personnel rushed onto the field to attend the receiver. Members of the Cincinnati roster left the sideline to gathered around their teammate, kneeling nearby as trainers continued their evaluations. Gibson’s parents eventually made their way to the field as well. The game was delayed 16 minutes as medical personnel stabilized Gibson, placed him on a stretcher, and transported out of TDECU Stadium. His father accompanied him on the back of the medical cart. Gibson subsequently made his way to Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center. Before his departure, Cincinnati Athletics reported the receiver as “alert and moving all extremities.” “Our personnel did an amazing job to get out there very quickly, they were right on top of JV,” Cincinnati head coach Scott Satterfield said in the immediate aftermath of the game. “Ultimately, they got him in a good place there. He was moving all four extremities on command. They took him to the hospital for precautionary reasons, and obviously they got to do their CT scans and those type of things. I don’t have an update, but hopefully everything checks out great. I thought JV was playing awesome tonight and unfortunately that happened to him. Prayers go out to JV and his family, but it’s a blessing for him to move all four extremities. It’s always very scary, and scary for our team.” In a later update, Cincinnati’s official Twitter account confirmed that Gibson had been discharged from Memorial Hermann-Texas Medical Center and traveled back to Cincinnati with the team.

sports.title: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories
sports.description: Real Madrid rediscover collective identity under Mourinho with eight consecutive victories Real Madrid have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past month, and the results have been there for everyone to see. Los Blancos secured a 3-0 victory over Valencia at Mestalla last night to make it eight wins in their last eight games. Jose Mourinho’s tactical modifications have worked wonders for the Spanish club, and the performances have also improved. According to MARCA , he has moulded the team into a more cohesive and disciplined unit after a difficult start to his second spell in the Spanish capital. Mourinho’s Real Madrid growing stronger collectively Madrid have scored 24 goals across those eight matches, averaging three per game, while keeping three clean sheets. The winning run includes victories over Barcelona in El Clasico and Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens in the Champions League. Saturday’s 3-0 victory over Valencia offered another example of their progress, with the team breaking down a resolute defensive unit. Jose Mourinho has galvanized the team at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) Los Che actually started the game very well, causing problems for Madrid, but goals from Fede Valverde, Arda Guler and Kylian Mbappe helped Mourinho’s men secure the three points. The most encouraging aspect of Real Madrid’s evolution is that the team no longer seem excessively dependent on individual brilliance. Mbappe, Guler, Diomande and Bellingham have come together to form an excellent attacking quartet, and their strengths complement each other perfectly. Mourinho’s defensive demands making the difference There was one moment in the Valencia game that perfectly summed up the defensive transformation under Mourinho. When Guler was caught out of position after Madrid lost possession, Mbappe sprinted across to cover the exposed space and restore the team’s defensive shape. One of the biggest criticisms levelled at the Frenchman was that he was not contributing enough defensively. How will Mourinho integrate Vinicius into the team? (Photo by Diego Souto/Getty Images) That has changed now, with everyone willing to put the team ahead of themselves. Mourinho will love the fact that his side have almost reached that stage. It remains to be seen how the dynamics change once Vinicius Jr. returns from suspension and how the manager reintegrates him. If the team can find a way for Vinicius to thrive within this system too, they could become even more devastating in the coming months. It remains to be seen how Mourinho handles his return.

sports.title: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent
sports.description: Barcelona new signing has a point to prove against Atletico Madrid after poor precedent Barcelona travel to the Metropolitano this weekend for one of the most important matches of the season. It promises to be an important game for many of the Barcelona players, including the new signing Anthony Gordon, who will play his first competitive game at the Metropolitano. Barcelona’s poor record against Atleti last season has already been well-documented , but this particular game is even more important for Gordon, who has had a bad precedent as well. The poor precedent Can Gordon make an impact against Atletico Madrid? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) As reported by Diario SPORT , Gordon has faced Atletico Madrid only once in his career. It was in August last year in the Sepa Cup, and it wasn’t the best of experiences for the winger. Deployed through the middle as Newcastle United slipped to a 2-0 defeat, it was a bruising afternoon for Gordon. The Englishman found fierce resistance from the Atleti defence and was eventually forced off in the 85th minute due to ankle discomfort. This could be an early reminder that Diego Simeone’s men could employ the same method when it comes to putting a halt to Gordon in the final third. This time, however, the Barcelona player will operate from the flanks, which should give the Englishman a higher degree of freedom. Pressure slowly growing Godon needs to up his performances once again. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) With three goals and five assists in all competitions, it will be perhaps unfair to criticise Gordon’s performances since joining Barcelona in the summer. The winger has won his battle with Karim Adeyemi for the left wing role, and established himself as a first-team regular. Yet, question marks remain. Gordon notably endured a poor outing against Real Madrid in the season’s first El Clasico and is still yet to score his first away goal in La Liga. His only goals in La Liga so far have come at home against Getafe and Alaves. That is quite a modest tally for a player of his quality. A strong performance against Atletico Madrid, to that end, could serve as an ideal confidence-booster for the former Newcastle United starlet, as he looks to solidify his role in Flick’s setup.

The loss officially means UNLV is no longer in control of its own destiny in regards to the Mountain West championship game, and a loss to New Mexico next week would likely all but eliminate the Rebels from contention. “Obviously, extremely disappointed in our performance tonight,” said UNLV head coach Dan Mullen. “We got a lot of issues, a lot of things we got to fix.” There were many culprits for the loss, but one of the major sticking points was UNLV being unable to stop the run. For the third straight week, the Rebels defense allowed the opponent to run the ball at will, with Wyoming putting up 351 net rushing yards. sports.title: Austin Reaves predicted Luka Doncic’s 40-point scoring tear over a year before Lakers star delivered
sports.description: Photo by Luke Hales/Getty Images Austin Reaves appears to have known exactly what Luka Doncic was capable of, with a prediction he made more than a year ago resurfacing as the Lakers star enjoys a remarkable start to the 2026-27 NBA season. Doncic is averaging 40.1 points through his first 10 games, helping Los Angeles move to an 8-2 record and the top of the Western Conference. The six-time All-Star has been particularly impressive over his last four outings, scoring 45, 42, 40 and 53 points as the Lakers recorded four consecutive wins. Austin Reaves predicted Luka Doncic could average 40 points for Los Angeles Lakers ESPN reporter Dave McMenamin recently brought attention to an old article featuring Reaves’ prediction that Doncic could average 40 points per game while still helping the Lakers win. At the time, Doncic had already shown what he could produce offensively, recording 91 points across two games to average 45.5, although Los Angeles split those contests. Reaves’ prediction now looks remarkably accurate, with Doncic leading the league in scoring while the Lakers continue to win. His efficiency has also been impressive. Doncic is shooting 49.8 per cent from the field and 41.9 per cent from three-point range, both career-high figures. The Slovenian is contributing beyond scoring, too, averaging 7.8 rebounds, 7.7 assists and 1.7 steals per game. His dominance is reflected across several other statistical categories. Doncic leads the NBA in field goals made and attempted, three-pointers made and attempted, as well as free throws made and attempted. He is currently making 12.2 field goals from 24.6 attempts per game, alongside 5.8 three-pointers from 13.8 attempts and 9.9 free throws from 11.3 attempts. However, the Lakers could face a concern ahead of their next outing against the Detroit Pistons. Doncic was listed as questionable on the front end of a back-to-back, potentially leaving Los Angeles without its leading scorer as it looks to extend its four-game winning streak. Another bowler-friendly track at Seddon Park is a real possibility, but the final answer may depend as much on the clouds over Hamilton as on the strip itself. The third ODI between New Zealand and India is scheduled for Tuesday, 10 November, with the first ball due at 3:00 PM local time (NZDT), which is 7:30 AM in India. India lead the five-match series 2-0, and both wins came on pitches that suited the fast bowlers. New Zealand were sent in twice and were unable to bat out 41 overs on either occasion, as the ball moved off the seam and the bounce was steep and at times uneven. At Seddon Park, head groundsman Karl Johnson is working through a difficult build-up. A tractor-mounted machine called a verti-drain has been rumbling over the outfield, punching holes into the grass with its tines so that the ground gets more air and drains faster if the rain returns, as more rain is expected on Monday and Tuesday. The early expectation is for a more balanced surface than the ones seen in Auckland and Wellington, although the weather could still keep the seamers interested. The ODIs, in contrast, were low-scoring and dominated by the bowlers. He said the aim is to prepare a surface that stays consistent for 100 overs with minimal seam movement, but the unsettled conditions have made that harder. “New Zealand’s been pretty wet over the last few days, and we’ve had quite a lot of rain here yesterday, so we’ve lost out some time but we’ve been able to get the pitch ready,” he said in an interview wth Cricinfo. science.description: NASA announced its 2025 Astronaut Candidate Class on Sept. 22, 2025, at the agency’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. Credit: NASA/Helen Arase Vargas NASA is looking for the explorers who will help write the next chapter of human spaceflight. Applications are now open for the agency’s next class of astronauts, who will join NASA as America returns to the Moon, builds the Moon Base, and lays the groundwork for the first crewed missions to Mars. The next generation of astronauts will train to operate on the lunar surface, live and work beyond Earth, and take on missions that will push the boundaries of human exploration farther than ever before. U.S. citizens interested in joining the astronaut corps have until 11:59 p.m. EST Thursday, Dec. 3, to submit their completed application materials at: https://go.nasa.gov/3WyvlQi “This is an extraordinary time to join NASA’s astronaut corps,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The people we select could walk on the Moon, live and work at the Moon Base, and help pioneer the systems and operations that will ultimately carry crews to Mars. Those missions will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage. NASA’s astronaut corps has always called on remarkable Americans willing to take on extraordinary challenges in service to the nation. If you are ready to join that tradition, come help write the next chapter of humanity’s greatest adventure.” NASA expects to make its final selection in late 2027 to begin training as the next class of astronaut candidates. “The window is open. The mission is waiting. And the only thing missing from the greatest adventure humanity has ever embarked upon is you,” said NASA Deputy Administrator Matt Anderson. The agency last opened applications in 2024. From more than 8,000 applications, 10 astronaut candidates were selected in 2025 and are currently completing nearly two years of training. “For those who apply, becoming a NASA astronaut is more than a career opportunity,” said Scott Tingle, chief astronaut and chair of the Astronaut Selection Board at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston. “It is a chance to join a legacy of explorers who have pushed the boundaries of discovery and play a role in the missions that will shape humanity’s future in space. The next generation of astronaut candidates could help write history while inspiring future scientists, engineers, and explorers.” Since the 1960s, NASA has selected 370 people to train as astronaut candidates for its increasingly challenging missions. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 7, 1992: NASA launches Mars Global Surveyor, its 1st Mars mission in 20 years at the time, to map the Red Planet like never before
science.description: null On Nov. 7, 1996, NASA launched its Mars Global Surveyor mission. This was the first mission NASA sent to Mars in almost 20 years! The Mars Global Surveyor spacecraft was an orbiter. It transmitted data from NASA's Mars rovers Sojourner , Spirit and Opportunity back to Earth. The spacecraft also did a lot of its own science. It found surface channels on Mars that appeared to have been created by running water. Mars Global Surveyor looked at the south pole of Mars and saw signs of possible climate change. It also saw a mineral called hematite on Mars. Hematite usually forms in water. NASA then sent its Spirit and Opportunity rovers to look for the hematite, and both rovers found it near their landing sites. Mars Global Surveyor survived much longer than expected. But a space maneuver accidentally exposed one of its batteries to the sun, and the spacecraft lost power. It fell silent forever in November 2006 . NASA launches the Mars Global Surveyor to Mars on a Delta II rocket on Nov. 7, 1996. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered As the first successful Mars mission since the two Viking launches in 1975, Mars Global Surveyor ushered in a new era of exploration of the Red Planet, not only through its own contributions to orbit-based science, but by serving a relay for surface-based rovers. As such, it became a primary pipeline for multiple concurrent Mars missions. "The [Mars Global Surveyor] mission overhauled scientists' understanding of Mars by studying the entire Martian surface, atmosphere and interior. Major findings included dramatic evidence that water still flows on Mars in short bursts down hillside gullies, and the identification of water-related mineral deposits leading to selection of a Mars rover landing site for a subsequent mission," read a NASA description of the probe. Mars Global Surveyor sent back more than 240,000 images to Earth during its nine active years. Want more space history? science.title: Send your name to Saturn's moon Titan with NASA's upcoming Dragonfly mission
science.description: null We still may be some time away from sending humans to distant reaches of the solar system, but you can send your name to Saturn's moon Titan, which has the ingredients of life on its surface thanks to NASA's Dragonfly mission. Dragonfly is an SUV-sized nuclear-powered rotorcraft that NASA aims to launch towards Titan in 2028. The agency opened a special events page in late October to allow members of the public to put their name on the spacecraft. The names will be put upon a chip on Dragonfly during the spacecraft's assembly, and all names must be submitted before Jan. 15, 2027. The agency says that the mission has no "ordinary itinerary," as Dragonfly aims to between areas miles (or kilometers) apart after arriving on the surface in 2034. "Nearly a billion miles away, an extraordinary destination awaits. Titan has an atmosphere, rivers and lakes, seasons, sweeping dunes and a landscape rich in organic material," NASA officials wrote in the event page. "Upon arrival in 2034, Dragonfly will fly from place to place on this intriguing world to uncover clues about this remarkable moon, and the chemistry that could help us understand the ingredients for life." Dragonfly will be one of just a few flying crafts on another world, with the first being NASA's plucky Ingenuity mini-helicopter that arrived on Mars along with the still-running Perseverance rover in 2021. With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus. science.title: Record-breaking, fast-spinning magnet could help uncover new physics
science.description: Magnets can be made to levitate by the Meissner effect Science History Images / Alamy A tiny magnet that levitates within a superconductor trap may be the fastest spinning object visible to the naked eye, and one of the fastest spinning objects ever made. In the future, it could be used in experiments searching for mysterious dark matter particles and aid the development of quantum technologies. Superconductors are materials that conduct electricity with perfect efficiency, and they also expel any magnetic field that tries to permeate them – a phenomenon known as the Meissner effect. Because of this, a magnet placed above a superconductor experiences repulsive magnetic forces and starts to levitate. Tao Wang at the Agency for Science Technology and Research in Singapore and his colleagues have now set one such levitating magnet spinning at an unprecedently fast rate. Read more A miniature magnet rivals behemoths in strength for the first time The researchers used a spherical magnet made from neodymium, iron and boron that was about 30 micrometres wide, similar to the width of a fine human hair. They placed it in a cylindrical container made from lead, then enclosed that container in a chamber devoid of air, or a vacuum chamber. Advertisement Next, they used liquid helium to cool the whole setup to approximately -269°C (-452°F), only a few degrees above the coldest possible temperature . Under these extreme circumstances, lead behaved as a superconductor and the lack of air meant that the magnet could levitate within it without bumping into any particles. The team set the magnet spinning with a magnetic coil, ultimately pushing this tiny rotor to 138 million revolutions per minute. Wang says the magnet’s spinning was also very stable: it would take 17 days for its spinning speed to decrease by 50 per cent, something that would typically happen more quickly due to interactions between the magnet and its environment. “In terms of how many turns it makes before slowing down significantly, this is in the same league as the Earth’s spinning,” he says. “This, so far, is the fastest magnetically levitated rotor.” The record for the fastest rotating human-made object is also held by a levitated sphere, but that one was nano-sized, so invisible to the naked eye, and levitated by laser beams. The team has already successfully tested it as a gauge of vacuum at very low temperatures. Wang says this could be useful for builders of quantum computers, which often must be kept extremely cold and isolated in order to work. Heatwaves across the world have shocked scientists with their scale and severity in recent years, with heat extremes dramatically outstripping both historical records and the predictions of climate models. Read more Extreme heat is now making cities unlivable. How can we survive it? In the UK in 2022, temperatures exceeded 40°C (104 ° F) for the first time in history, despite predictions that such a milestone was probably still years away. Likewise, the 2021 heatwave in the Pacific Northwest saw temperatures hit extremes that far outstripped climate model projections. One team thinks the answer lies partly in the soil. Scientists already knew that high-pressure systems allow more solar radiation to reach Earth’s surface, heating up the land. They also knew that higher temperatures dry soils more quickly, removing the cooling effect provided by evaporation, thereby further amplifying heatwaves. This three-way feedback effect makes extreme heatwaves 10 per cent hotter than they would otherwise be, according to the research by Kornhuber and his colleagues – a factor not fully accounted for in climate model projections. science.title: You can see another galaxy with the naked eye — here's how to find it
science.description: null The first time I showed someone the Andromeda galaxy (M31), our conversation did not go quite as planned. I'd carefully worked my way across the sky, starting from the Great Square of Pegasus and hopping from star to star until I was confident I had the right patch. I pointed the telescope, got M31 in its crosshairs and proudly announced to my wife that I had found the closest giant galaxy to the Milky Way . Would she like to see it? She then stayed quiet for a little too long as she looked through the eyepiece. Then came an unexpected question. "Is it near that little smudge?" Hmmm. "Err, no. It is that little smudge," I replied. There was a pause. Of course, I knew exactly what had happened. We'd both seen photographs of M31 — a vast spiral galaxy with a brilliant center, sweeping dust lanes and hundreds of billions of stars. What we were actually looking at was a grayish blur that could easily have been mistaken for a mark on the eyepiece. That apparent disappointment is now my favorite part of finding Andromeda because the unimpressive smudge is real. The light entering your eyes has been traveling across space for about 2.5 million years. No screen, photograph or telescope is necessary. You are intercepting ancient light in your backyard. Technically, the Triangulum Galaxy (M33), about 2.7 million light-years away, can be seen with the naked eye, so it is therefore the most distant object the naked eye can see. But not mine — I've never seen it. M31 is a much more realistic naked-eye target. What's happening and when to look The Andromeda galaxy is at its most dramatic in photographs, not an eyepiece. (Image credit: Created using Canva and a base image from Starry Night) Early November is an excellent time to find M31 from the Northern Hemisphere. It's high and well placed during the evening, and this week the moon is becoming particularly cooperative. New Moon falls around Nov. 9, giving us several evenings with little or no moonlight to wash out faint deep-sky objects. I usually begin with the star Alpheratz, one of the corner stars of the Great Square of Pegasus. You go two stars left, two stars up, and you arrive at M31. Another route — and a good way to check you're in the right place — starts in Cassiopeia, the distinctive W-shaped constellation high in the northeastern sky on autumn evenings. You can use its second V-shape as an arrow pointing straight at M31. You can do that star-hop with the naked eye or a pair of binoculars, but M31 is visible to the naked eye only under a very dark sky. However, don't look for a miniature version of the photographs. Expect a faint, elongated patch with a slightly brighter middle. There's another beginner trap to avoid. Images make Andromeda look compact, but its full apparent extent is enormous — several times the width of the full moon — and our eyes usually pick up only the much brighter central region.
